clue.text: Head of secondary school's an excessively studious type

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of secondary
a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: A head teacher at a secondary school is a bookish swot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of secondary school' reads as a headteacher, but school is the group of whales. SPOD is British slang for a dull, studious person.
explanation.definitionFit: Spod is British informal slang for a boring, overly bookish person, a swot or nerd.

clue.text: Question a way to present a doomed queen

blocks.note: how is a question word
taken as written
RD, short for road, a way

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the best way to stage a play about a tragic queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Catherine Howard, fifth wife of Henry VIII, was beheaded in 1542.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine Howard was an English queen consort executed for adultery, so she was a doomed queen.

clue.text: Overbearing drunk had to accept sorry end

indicators.note: something in a sorry state is a mess, so these letters are jumbled
to accept something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: high means intoxicated
taken as written
the letters of end, rearranged

explanation.surface: A bullying drunk was forced to accept a miserable fate.
explanation.walkthrough: Drunk looks like the definition next to Overbearing, but it is wordplay; sorry signals only the short word end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone high-handed acts in an arrogant, domineering way, which is to be overbearing.

clue.text: Sense alien is circling island — creature from the depths?

indicators.note: alien means strange or foreign, so the letters take a strange new order
to circle something is to surround it, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: the letters of sense, rearranged
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial senses something circling an island: a sea monster rising?
explanation.walkthrough: Nessie is the nickname of the Loch Ness Monster in Scotland; the question mark flags that she may not exist.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessie is the legendary monster said to live deep in Loch Ness, a creature from the depths.

clue.text: Drink in bed provoked a tense player's stroke

indicators.note: letters that are provoked are stirred up, so they are put into a new order
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
taken as written
taken as written
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Being given a drink in bed made a tense musician lash out.
explanation.walkthrough: The drink is placed after the first letter of the jumble. The player is a drummer, and stroke is a single hit, not an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A drumbeat is a single hit on a drum, the stroke a percussion player makes.

clue.text: Thumb book: Sepulchre

blocks.note: Tom is the first name of Tom Thumb, the tiny folk-tale hero
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Leaf through a book with your thumb and find the word sepulchre.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb is a thumb-sized boy from English folklore, so Thumb calls up his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepulchre is a burial chamber, which is what a tomb is.

clue.text: Discerning person put off holding court ball

indicators.note: a thing holding something has it inside, so the other pieces sit within

blocks.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
CT is the abbreviation for court
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A perceptive player was put off by holding the ball on court.
explanation.walkthrough: Court ball looks like one sporting item, but court and ball are separate pieces, each abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A detector is someone or something that discovers or perceives, so a discerning person in the literal sense.

clue.text: Joint provided by Kennedy's firstborn

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the name before it

blocks.note: the first letter of Kennedy
née means born, used before a maiden name

explanation.surface: A cannabis joint was supplied by the Kennedy family's eldest son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firstborn' reads as one word for eldest child; split it into first and born.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the joint between the thigh and the lower leg.

clue.text: Academic with a special quality — always diminished as an exploiter

indicators.note: diminished means made smaller, so a letter is lost from the word

blocks.note: prof, short for professor
it is that indefinable special quality, as in 'she's got it'
ever means always

explanation.surface: A charismatic professor, ever more reduced, ends up taking advantage of others.
explanation.walkthrough: EVER loses its V to become the poetic contraction E'ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A profiteer makes excessive gains by exploiting shortages or others' needs.

clue.text: Some lines about cinema

blocks.note: an ode is a poem, a set of lines
on can mean concerning, about

explanation.surface: A few remarks about the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: Odeon is a well-known chain of British cinemas.
explanation.definitionFit: An Odeon is a cinema, from the British chain name that became a general word for picture houses.

clue.text: Lifelike cast? Yes and no

blocks.note: surface reading: a realistic sculpture or a convincing set of actors
setter's reading: the mould is true to the face but taken after life has ended

explanation.walkthrough: The plaster mould is taken from a face just after death, so it is lifelike in likeness but not in its subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A death mask is a cast made of a person's face after they die, faithful in features yet lifeless.

clue.text: Note house beer's off around five

indicators.note: beer that is off has gone bad, so its letters are spoiled into a new order
around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, a common British home
the letters of beer, rearranged
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A note: the beer in the house has gone off, by about five.
explanation.definitionFit: A semibreve is a musical note, the whole note lasting four beats.

clue.text: Aim to take hunted animals when mating is imminent?

blocks.note: an end is an aim or goal
game is wild animals hunted for sport

explanation.surface: A hunter's goal is to bag animals during the breeding season.
explanation.walkthrough: Mating looks like breeding animals, but it is checkmate in chess.
explanation.definitionFit: The endgame is the last stage of a chess match, when checkmate is close at hand.

clue.text: Country dancing finally commandeered by criminal type

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it
criminal means crooked or bent, so the letters are twisted out of order
something commandeered is seized and held, so it ends up inside the other piece

blocks.note: the last letter of dancing
the letters of type, rearranged

explanation.surface: Folk dancing has been taken over by a shady character.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a country in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Expressions of hesitation about telltale's slip

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hesitation sounds wrap around the other piece

blocks.note: er and um are both sounds made while hesitating
to rat is to tell tales, an informer is a rat

explanation.surface: A stammering informer lets something slip.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in printing or writing, a slip of the pen.

clue.text: Revival of Greece runs out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of place and need rearranging

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Greece's revival runs out of steam.
explanation.definitionFit: A resurgence is a rise again after a decline, which is a revival.

clue.text: 'Quiet, dear' is an example of preservation

blocks.note: to keep mum is to stay quiet
my, like dear, is an exclamation of surprise, as in 'oh my!'

explanation.surface: A parent hushes a child: 'Quiet, dear'.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a mother speaking, which is a joke, since mummy is also British for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: An Egyptian mummy is a body embalmed and wrapped to preserve it, an instance of preservation.

clue.text: Bear in cave (if switched round)

blocks.note: first meaning: to produce, as a tree bears fruit
second meaning: once the two words are switched round they read cave in, to give way

explanation.surface: A bear sheltering in a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket tells you to swap in and cave, turning 'in cave' into the phrase cave in, which means to give way.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is both to produce a crop or return and to give way under pressure or surrender.

clue.text: Wishes to dispose of capital income

indicators.note: the capital is the opening letter, and disposing of it means it is dropped

blocks.note: yearnings are longings or wishes

explanation.surface: Someone wants to sell off their capital to provide income.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital looks financial, but it means the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are money received for work or from investment, an income.

clue.text: That's remiss, whichever way you view it

indicators.note: a word that reads the same from either end looks identical whichever way you view it

blocks.note: the click of disapproval said at a lapse

explanation.surface: A complaint that something was careless, however you look at it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tut is an exclamation of disapproval, the sound made on noticing someone's carelessness.

clue.text: It could help in making a child try a transport system

definitions.text: It could help in making a child

blocks.note: to test is to try
the Tube is London's underground railway

explanation.surface: Something that might help a child try out a train network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a child' points to IVF: a test-tube baby is conceived outside the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Laboratory glassware used in IVF, giving the phrase test-tube baby, so it can help in conceiving a child.

clue.text: Get away from studio head and press

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of studio
to cram is to press or pack tightly

explanation.surface: Escape from the head of the studio and the reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: Studio head reads as a film boss, and press as journalists; both are false.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is an informal command to leave quickly, so it means get away.

clue.text: Being without oxygen somehow deters shipworms

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive by some unstated route, in a new order
being without here means being outside, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
the letters of deters, rearranged

explanation.surface: Being starved of oxygen somehow keeps shipworms at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: Without usually means lacking, but here it is the older sense outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Teredo is the genus name of the shipworm, a wood-boring mollusc, and teredos is its plural.

clue.text: Bob Short? OK on reflection!

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the word appears backwards

blocks.note: curt means short, abrupt
yes and OK are both words of agreement

explanation.surface: A man named Bob Short agrees, after a moment's thought.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob Short reads as a man's name; bob is the definition, a small bending of the knees.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtsey is a bob, the bending of the knees made as a respectful greeting.

clue.text: President's minder takes Trump's lead

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front letter, so only that one is used
to take something in is to hold it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a carer looks after someone, a minder
the first letter of Trump

explanation.surface: A presidential bodyguard follows Trump's lead.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy Carter was the 39th US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Jimmy Carter was President of the United States from 1977 to 1981.

clue.text: Poetic lines getting controversial treatment in collection

indicators.note: getting here means receiving, so one piece is taken within the other

blocks.note: a set is a collection
est, Erhard Seminars Training, was a controversial self-help therapy of the 1970s

explanation.surface: A poetry anthology is getting a contentious reception.
explanation.walkthrough: Treatment suggests the reception of a book; here it is a therapy, the 1970s self-improvement course known as est.
explanation.definitionFit: A sestet is a group of six lines of verse, such as the closing part of a sonnet.

clue.text: Player, chirpy thing, about to make a comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a coming back, so the word travels the other way

blocks.note: a cricket is an insect that chirps
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A cheerful sportsman is about to return to the team.
explanation.walkthrough: Chirpy looks like a mood, but it describes the noisy insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer is a player of cricket, the bat-and-ball game.

clue.text: Feature of Superman's head

blocks.note: first meaning: the red garment the hero wears over his shoulders
second meaning: a headland jutting into the sea

explanation.walkthrough: Superman's head suggests his face or hair; the 's is only a link, and head is the geographical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape is a sleeveless cloak, part of Superman's costume, and also a promontory, a head of land.

clue.text: Considering dropping spare member on board

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it go, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: thinking is considering
spare can mean lean or thin

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about letting a spare director go from the company board.
explanation.walkthrough: Board looks like a company board, but it is the chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The king is a chess piece, one of the members of the set on the board.

clue.text: Keep Somalian boxing course

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the letters are held inside the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A Somali fighter needs to keep up his boxing training course.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom is an English racecourse in Surrey, home of the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is a racecourse, so the name stands for a course.

clue.text: See 11
Heathen state taken by Greek god

indicators.note: something taken by another is held by it, so it goes inside

blocks.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and the wild
GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A godless nation is captured by a deity from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan is someone outside the main world religions, which is what heathen means.

clue.text: They clean the cheap seats

blocks.note: first meaning: people or agents that whiten things with chemicals
second meaning: the uncovered benches at an American sports ground

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests cleaners working in a stadium; the second sense is American.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleachers are things that bleach, and in US English the bare tiered benches at a ground.
